rachel: Starting a short thread for cust-lumin adapter bring-up onto oak-13b-v2.2. Quick-eval flagged vocab reshuffle + int4 regressions. Keeping notes here.
omar: TL;DR of the problem?
rachel: Their tokenizer adds <AMOUNT_USD> and <AMOUNT_EUR>, and reindexes a block of high ids. Naive merge left some currency symbols and decimals split into multiple subtokens -> detokenize spacing changes.
jin: Any runtime breakages after merging weights?
rachel: Yes, saw streaming inconsistencies with long contexts:
```
RuntimeError: kv_cache length mismatch: expected 10240 got 8192
  at runtime/kv_cache.cpp:159
```
Root cause: customer uses 10k context; model config stayed at 8192. Bumped model.config.max_position_embeddings to 10240 for local tests and playback fixed the crash.
mike: Numbers from the quick-eval pack? keep it concise.
rachel: Quickpack (invoice/amount extraction):
- oak-13b-v2.2 fp16 (baseline): EM=0.86, F1=0.93
- lumin-lora merged fp16: EM=0.85, F1=0.92
- lumin-lora merged int4 (per-channel asymmetric): EM=0.78, F1=0.88
Quantization is biggest EM drop. There's also small FP16 detokenize delta (~+/-0.01 EM) due to token id remap.
omar: Any concrete failing examples? small ones help.
rachel: Example A:
input: "Total due: €1.234,56 (incl VAT)"
baseline: "Total due: €1.234,56 (incl VAT)"
merged-fp16: "Total due: €1.234,56 (incl VAT)"
merged-int4: "Total due €1 234,56 included VAT"
Int4 removed punctuation and split the € token into [302, 7091] in the candidate tokenizer.
jin: Run token diff and paste the mapping snippet.
rachel: Token diff output (snippet):
```
€ => base:[3320] candidate:[302,7091]
"," => base:[45] candidate:[45]
"." => base:[12] candidate:[12]
```
So only the currency sign is split. Occurs ~0.25% of samples in quickpack.
token-bot: quick-eval token-drift rule triggered: token splits (>1 tokens) for high-frequency symbol '€' at 0.25% (> threshold 0.1%). See /artifacts/lumin/1767729991/token_drift.json
mike: Remediation options?
jin: Two practical paths: (1) force base tokenizer and reindex LoRA embeddings (accurate but needs re-saving weights + re-verification), (2) add preprocess collapse map that converts candidate-token sequences back to single logical tokens before detokenize and evaluation (fast). Also consider tiny QAT on LoRA params to recover quant loss.
omar: Did we run any quant sims?
rachel: Yes: ran quant_sim per-channel symmetric and asymmetric + a short QAT sim 400 steps on LoRA only. eval artifacts attached.
token-bot: quant_sim summary: symmetric int4 EM delta = -0.10; asymmetric int4 EM delta = -0.06; QAT (400 steps) projected EM delta = -0.03. Full logs: /artifacts/lumin/1767729991/quant_sim.json
mike: Short-term rollout plan?
jin: Propose canary merged-fp16 at 5% on dedicated pool so customers don't see int4 issues. Block int4 until QAT or remerge gets EM within 0.03. Add fallback when EM_drop >= 0.04.
omar: Agree. Also add a quick token-diff check to preflight so merges that introduce splits for currency or punctuation >0.1% get flagged.
rachel: I pushed a quick preprocess that collapses known split sequences for currency symbols (e.g., [302,7091] -> €) and re-ran int4 quickpack: EM improved 0.78 -> 0.80. Better but not at fp16 yet. Patch: github.com/redwood-inference/customer-onboards/issues/4392.
mike: Action items: (1) rachel: expand preprocess map + rerun short evals, (2) jin: run token-aligned LoRA reindex experiment and QAT longer run, (3) omar: start fp16 canary (5%) and configure fallback EM_drop>=0.04 sliding 1k requests, (4) add token-diff preflight rule (jin/omar).
canary-bot: Canary request received. Will post deploy when live.
canary-bot: Canary deployed: lumin-lora-fp16 -> dedicated/pool-5 (5%). Fallback: EM_drop>=0.04 -> revert to oak-13b-v2.2. Monitoring: /console/canaries/lumin/1767729991
mike: Holding on int4 rollout until QAT or reindex shows acceptable metrics. Reopen thread with quant/QAT artifacts. Thanks all :thumbsup:
